# @engineering-os/monorepo — Engineering OS Managed

This repository uses Engineering OS (EOS) as its knowledge layer. Codex should use EOS MCP tools for project context instead of rediscovering architecture, conventions, decisions, and dependency relationships from scratch.

## Mandatory EOS MCP usage

| When you want to... | Use this EOS tool | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| Understand the project before starting | `eos_context` | Broad manual exploration |
| Find where something is implemented | `eos_search` | Ad hoc grep/find scans |
| Check architecture/service boundaries | `eos_architecture` | Inferring from random files |
| Know conventions to follow | `eos_conventions` | Guessing from nearby code |
| Check if a decision was already made | `eos_recall_decision` | Re-debating settled choices |
| See what depends on what | `eos_dependencies` | Manually tracing imports |
| Check impact before changing an interface | `eos_impact` | Hoping nothing breaks |
| Find coding patterns to follow | `eos_patterns` | Creating a new pattern by default |
| Plan implementation work | `eos_plan` | Creating a plan from scratch |
| Validate code against standards | `eos_validate` | Manual-only review |
| Run security review | `eos_security_scan` | Manual OWASP check |
| Remember a durable codebase lesson | `eos_learn` | Letting it disappear after the session |
| Recall learned skills/gotchas | `eos_recall_skills` | Rediscovering past lessons |

## Rules

1. Call `eos_context` first before starting implementation or review work.
2. Prefer `eos_search` for project lookup before broad filesystem exploration.
3. Call `eos_recall_decision` before introducing or changing architecture decisions.
4. Call `eos_impact` before changing shared interfaces, public APIs, or cross-service contracts.
5. Follow `eos_conventions`; do not infer conventions when EOS has a recorded rule.
6. Call `eos_patterns` before adding new utilities, abstractions, or repeated structures.
7. Call `eos_learn` when you discover a durable gotcha, convention, or project-specific connection.
8. Call `eos_recall_skills` near the start of substantial tasks to reuse prior learning.

## Codex review guidelines

- For `@codex review`, prioritize P0/P1 bugs, security regressions, broken contracts, and behavior changes that violate EOS decisions or conventions.
- Use `eos_impact` when a diff touches exported types, schemas, APIs, package boundaries, or shared infrastructure.
- Use `eos_security_scan` or `eos_security_audit` for security-sensitive changes.

## EOS Codex skills

Repo-scoped EOS workflows live under `.agents/skills/eos-*`. Invoke them explicitly with `$eos-plan`, `$eos-review`, `$eos-security`, etc., or let Codex choose them when the task matches their descriptions.
